body:
When one gradually refines thought for entry into the nature just stated, the contemplation-course preceded by true reasoning, good scripture, and good teacher-teaching has use. Thought-force alone binds beings (the conceit "I am bound" is saṃsāra's lock); adversarial thought shatters it — that is the cause of rising. The adversarial thought's form: transcending all limited Śiva-ending principles is unlimited consciousness-only — the ultimate, thing-order-ground, universe's vigor, "I am" (universe-transcending and universe-self). It does not arise for the Māyā-blind (no true reasoning). Vaiṣṇavas are confined by passion-principle in their scripture and hate the reasoning that would turn them (scripture quote). Only Śāmbhava-firm-descent-pierced enter by good-scripture course. The objection "would this make the supreme thought-formed?" is dissolved: thought's fulfillment is merely shattering duality-habitation; the supreme self-shines everywhere — thought neither aids nor refutes. For the very-firmly-pierced, true reasoning rises spontaneously — "Goddess-initiated." Others come by scripture-course (details later). The teacher expounds scripture; scripture raises fitting thought born of unhesitating study — that is true reasoning, and it is contemplation (making the dim brilliant). No other yoga-limb is a direct means (austerity, restraint, non-harm, yama, filling, breath-control handle knowables, not consciousness). Withdrawal heightens senses; meditation/concentration/absorption grant object-identity. Practice in the supreme nature is impossible (bundle-carrying analogy; in awareness there is nothing to take or remove). Reasoning's sole job: removing duality-habitation.

The passage moves in seven steps. (1) Bondage-conceit and its shattering. (2) The ultimate formula (unlimited consciousness-only). (3) Vaiṣṇava fence + quote. (4) Goddess-initiated spontaneous reasoning vs scripture course. (5) Teacher/scripture division. (6) Yoga-limb demotion (tapaḥ/restraint/yama/breath handle knowables; pratyāhāra heightens senses; dhyāna grants identity). (7) Practice-impossibility (bundle analogy; nothing to take/remove) + tarka's sole job (removing duality-habitation) + worldly practice parallel.
terms: sattarka (true reasoning), bhāvanā (contemplation), vikalpa (thought), dvaitādhivāsa (duality-habitation), śuddhavidyā (pure knowledge), pratyāhāra (withdrawal).
see_also: A03 (śāmbhava), A05 (āṇava), essay0 Q3 ("What keeps me bound?"), spans TS4.1–4.17.
function: Establishes the śākta upāya (thought-work): true reasoning as direct means, yoga-limbs demoted, practice impossible in the supreme.
local_context: A03 (śāmbhava) precedes; A04 teaches thought-refinement; A05 (āṇava) follows.
boundary: Descent-manifestation details deferred (śaktipātaprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ). Sarvajñānottara argument (4.44) external. vivaraṇa/stotra cross-refs external.

body:
Even ordinary practice proves the point: you picture the liked form as awareness and un-picture the rest — that is all practice ever was. In the supreme there is nothing to reject (duality-habitation is mere non-recognition, not a separate entity). The ultimate shines forth by stages (budding → blooming → bloomed); that shining is the Lord's nature. So no yoga-limbs as straight means. True reasoning — graced reasoning — is the straight means: pure knowledge, refined manifoldly into five shapes: sacrifice (offering all into the Lord — outer flowers for the lovely-minded), fire-offering (dissolving all into Lord-fire), muttering (inner grasping "that supreme is own-nature"), vow (seeing body/pot with Lord-identity; Nandiśikhā: all-sameness = supreme vow), yoga (staying in the shining). The Lord is full awareness; his fullness is power — clan, might, wave, heart, pith, throb, glory, triple-peak, Kālī, dragger, Fierce, Speech, enjoyment, sight, ever-fresh — named by āgama-tongues. Seen whole-powered, that fullness shines as conviction. His powers are past counting. Three contain it: supreme power (holding-seeing-shining everything from Śiva to earth as bare awareness), supreme-nonsupreme (mirror-elephant, difference-nondifference), nonsupreme (mutually fenced-apart difference). The embrace that swallows all three back into itself, recollecting inward, is goddess Parā herself (Mātṛsadbhāva, Kālakarṣiṇī).

The passage has two movements. First, the revaluation: ordinary practice = picturing liked forms as awareness; in the supreme, nothing to reject; duality-habitation = non-recognition; the ultimate shines by stages; no yoga-limbs as straight means; true reasoning is the straight means (pure knowledge), refined into five shapes with their intents (sacrifice: offering all into the Lord; fire-offering: dissolving all into Lord-fire; muttering: inner grasping; vow: Lord-identity seeing; yoga: staying in the shining). Second, the three powers: the Lord is full awareness named by āgama-tongues; three contain it (parā/parāpara/aparā); the holder is Parā herself.
terms: śuddhavidyā (pure knowledge), yāga (sacrifice), homa (fire-offering), japa (muttering), vrata (vow), parā/parāpara/aparā (three powers), Parā (holder).
function: Reinterprets outer rites as inner thought-gestures; establishes the three powers and their holder.
local_context: P1 established sattarka; P2 shows how rites become inner.
boundary: Name-etymologies per āgama (external). 4.27–4.33 detail in cut but summarized.

body:
Four powers, each going threefold (autonomy) = twelve, for creating, keeping, unmaking. The kalana demonstration: awareness grasps inward, then outward, affection, re-absorption-will, doubt-making-and-swallowing, consumer-nature, vessel-traces, sense-wheel, sense-lords, Māyā-knower, contracted-then-expanding knower, expanded form — twelve goddess-consciousnesses, aimed at one or many, together or in turn, revolving like seasons, nourishing wheel-lord autonomy = Kālīs. Kalana = motion/throwing/knowing/counting/enjoying/sounding/self-dissolving (Bhūtirāja quote). The full sense lives in the author's longer works (vivaraṇa/prakaraṇa/stotra); neither blab everywhere nor hide totally (teachers' rule). So "sacrifice and the rest" means: in a Maheśvara like this. All from Viṣṇu to Śiva treat the rejectable as adoptable-ground — false view, must be dropped by unsurpassed yogins (Anubhavastotra's zeal). In yāga-to-yoga pentads each manifoldly established — practice as established, not by food/purity discriminations (impurity isn't thing-nature like blue; Śiva-command alone overrides, proven by reason + endless āgamas — Tantrāloka for detail). Vedic-to-Kula rules alike do nothing here.

The passage has two movements. First, the twelve-Kālī demonstration: four powers × threefold = twelve, with the full kalana sequence (grasping inward → outward → affection → re-absorption → doubt → consumer → vessel → sense-wheel → sense-lords → Māyā-knower → contracted/expanding → expanded). Second, the conduct rule: kalana = motion/knowing/enjoying (Bhūtirāja); teachers' secrecy rule; "sacrifice and the rest" = in a Maheśvara; false view (rejectable as adoptable); Anubhavastotra's zeal; purity is not thing-nature (blue analogy); Śiva-command overrides (reason + endless āgamas); Tantrāloka for detail; Vedic-to-Kula rules ineffective.
terms: kālī (twelve goddesses), kalana (grasping/motion), Bhūtirāja (authority quote), Anubhavastotra (zeal), śivacodanā (Śiva-command).
function: Completes the powers doctrine (twelve Kālīs) and the conduct rule (purity-rules void; Śiva-command overrides).
local_context: P1 established sattarka; P2 inner rites; P3 completes powers + conduct.
boundary: vivaraṇa/stotra cross-refs (external). Tantrāloka detail (external). Bhūtirāja quote assumed.
